title: Every looping ACE song has a hard splice at the loop point: ace_import.seamless() silently drops the crossfade join
repro: Proof 1 (synthetic): ffmpeg aevalsrc ramp 0.04*t, 20 s -> ace_import.seamless('r.wav','rj.wav',3.0) gives 14.0 s (expected 17.0); last sample = original t=17, first = original t=3, so the '[tail][head]acrossfade' join is empty (ffmpeg 6.1.1: acrossfade of two atrim'd 3 s inputs with d=3 outputs nothing, even d=2.99; concat then emits only the body). Proof 2 (shipped files): boss_wyrm raw chosen 109.1 s, trimmed 108.0, ogg 102.0 (expected 105.0); combat_light 98.2->92.2, mega_iron 121.2->115.2, bowling_alley 115.7->109.7: every ogg is trimmed-6 s. Proof 3 (audible clicks): decoded last/first samples farm 0.592 -> -0.111 (99th pct sample step 0.069, i.e. a ~10x step = pop every loop), mine_deep 0.415->0.067, clinic -0.171->0.257, rain 0.073->0.309, mine 0.461->-0.067, town 0.010->-0.462, shop 0.374->-0.164, night, moon, wastes, boss_penguin, mega_frost, ruins, bowling_alley, meadow (second-difference spike at the join 4-49x the track's 99.9th pct). Besides the pop, every loop is a hard cut from 3 s before the end to 3 s after the start: mid-bar, mid-chord, beat grid broken (onset periodicity across the join drops vs mid-song: night 0.14 vs 0.57, farm 0.38 vs 0.75, rain 0.30 vs 0.67, lake 0.23 vs 0.55, forest 0.21 vs 0.47, mega_gloam 0.35 vs 0.70, mega_desert_canyon, meadow, docks, house, colony_coral, sky). Root cause narrowed: in ffmpeg 6.1.1 acrossfade fed by atrim branches of the same input (with or without asplit, any d: 1, 2.9, 3) outputs nothing; the same crossfade on two separate WAV files (-ss 17 -t 3 / -t 3) correctly outputs 3.0 s.
fix: Minimal fix: in seamless() cut head/tail/body to three temp WAVs first (ffmpeg -ss/-t or atrim per file), then acrossfade the two files and concat body+join (verified working on separate files); or do it in numpy. 1) Rewrite seamless() as a sample-accurate numpy crossfade (decode to float, out = concat(body[x:d-x], tail*fade_out + head*fade_in) with equal-power curves, write WAV) instead of the ffmpeg filtergraph; better still snap the splice to a beat: pick x near 3 s where onset envelopes of head/tail align (cross-correlate the two onset envelopes, shift tail by the best lag within +-0.5 s). 2) Add a self-check in ace_import after encoding: decoded |x[-1]-x[0]| < 3*p99(|diff|) and duration == trimmed - xfade (+-20 ms), else fail. 3) Add tools/music_loop_check.py (in check.sh): for every non-ONCE audio/music/*.ogg, fail if the join's second-difference > 4x the track's 99.9th pct. 4) Repair the shipped files: re-import from raw where present (/home/claude/work/ace_raw has 44 of them; sandbox only), otherwise re-download by song id from audio/ACE_LOG.json (download_song) or, as a fallback, run the fixed seamless on the current ogg itself (current file = original[3:d-3], so one more crossfade of its own ends is musically fine; one extra q2 generation). Log --reimport-all in ACE_LOG notes.
audio_needed: none (re-import of existing renders; re-downloads by id if raw files are gone)

title: False endings / dead air inside loops: ACE render ended, then a fragment restarted, and the trim kept both
repro: 0.5 s RMS windows more than 18 dB under the track median, inside the song (s:dB, median ~-15): quarry 132.5-133.5 s down to -62 dB (song is 143 s: a full stop then a 9 s fragment loops back; biggest 0.5 s step 46 dB), hideout 128.0-128.5 (-43, of 140 s), battle_gang 105.0-105.5 (-40, of 112 s, in the middle of a fight), danger 128 (-40, of 141), docks 10.5 and 133.5-136 (-37), finargle 115.5-117 (-37, of 130), mine 115.5-117.5 (-37), campaign_map 25-27 s and 71.5-75.5 s (-34..-39: two 2-4 s near-silences on the board screen), house 62.5-63 (-41), mine_deep 76 (-38). ace_pick's holes check only counts < median-30 dB, so these pass; trim_quiet only trims the very end.

Re-import the 11 tracks listed (raw by id from ACE_LOG) and re-listen. campaign_map's two mid breaks are probably arrangement breaks: if kept, at least the loop must not land in one; otherwise re-render (see weakest-songs list).

title: Loops restart on a quiet intro: 7-12 dB dip every loop on 12 songs; use loop_offset so the intro plays once
repro: RMS of the file's first 3 s vs last 3 s (dB): mine 12.2, boss 11.0, moon 10.7, boss_gang 9.8, chapel 8.8, mega_wind_storm 8.3, underground 8.0, battle_siege 7.5, mega_desert 7.4, boss_light_eater 7.4, mine_deep 7.2, title_musicbox 7.2; first 50 ms vs last 50 ms e.g. colony_ember -50.3 vs -15.9, mega_desert -51.7 vs -18.1, hideout -45.5 vs -33.0, underground -35.1 vs -11.3, mountain -36.7 vs -29.7 (head 15 dB under the median). Every loop the song drops to its soft intro and builds again: in boss/battle songs (boss, boss_gang, battle_siege, boss_light_eater) the fight music collapses every 1.5-2 min.
fix: ace_import computes the intro end (first 0.5 s window within 3 dB of the median after the head, snapped to the nearest strong onset) and writes it to a generated data/music_loops.json {track: loop_offset_s}; Music sets (stream as AudioStreamOggVorbis).loop_offset = that value next to loop = true (line ~117). The seamless crossfade then joins the tail to the loop_offset point instead of t=0. Keeps the intro for first entry, removes the dip.
